articles.title: Chingalán, baja de última hora en Kuwait por lesión de Galán
articles.standfirst: Según ha podido saber MARCA Pádel el español no se ha recuperado a tiempo de una leve lesión que no le impedirá estar en el Mundial con España en pocos días.
articles.summary: Según ha podido saber MARCA Pádel el español no se ha recuperado a tiempo de una leve lesión que no le impedirá estar en el Mundial con España en pocos días.
articles.body: chingalán es baja de última hora para el Major de Kuwait por una leve lesión del español de la que no ha podido recuperarse a tiempo para el tercer grande de la temporada de Premier Padel. Una noticia que ha podido conocer MARCA Pádel a lo largo de la tarde y que ha acabado por confirmar el propio Galán a través de sus redes sociales lamentando no poder participar en la cita de Kuwait, torneo del que se proclamó campeón la pasada temporada junto a Chingotto en el Mundial por parejas de la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP). Según ha podido saber este periódico el español no se ha recuperado de una lesión que todavía no se ha hecho pública, pero que no le impedirá estar en el Mundial que se celebra en pocos días para defender la camiseta de España. De esta forma el número uno masculino de la temporada queda sentenciado y los Golden Boys, Agustín Tapia y Arturo Coello, firmarán en 2026 su tercera temporada consecutiva en Premier Padel como números uno a la que habría que sumar el número uno logrado en 2023 en World Padel Tour. Una pareja lucky loser será la agraciada en cubrir la ausencia de la pareja dos en el torneo de Kuwait abriendo, de esta forma por ranking, la posibilidad de una nueva final a la pareja cuatro, Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk, que mandan en el cuadro por la parte baja.

articles.title: Littler reaches last eight as Van Veen exits Euros
articles.summary: Littler reaches last eight as Van Veen exits Euros
articles.body:
Luke Littler had a three-dart average of 114.47 as he beat Nathan Aspinall in the last 16 of the European Championship, while defending champion Gian van Veen was knocked out.

World champion Littler raced into a 4-0 lead in Dortmund and, while Aspinall recovered to 5-4, he won the best-of-19 match 10-5.

"I felt really good from the off," 19-year-old Littler told ITV. "I was gutted I gave him that leg going into the break at 4-1 - I wanted 5-0.

"But, as Nathan does, he's always there and is going to come back at you so I couldn't afford to drop off."

Littler has faced hostile treatment in Germany in the past and there was an incident midway through his match against Aspinall which caused a short pause in play.

"Just before I went for bull on the 126, the front table just decided to bang really loud on the table," said the world number one.

"The guy that did it looked up, I pointed at him and said, 'That's you'.

"Then he just picked up his pen, started writing on his little 180 card and didn't look up. So, he knew what he'd done.

"But that's the first thing all weekend, the crowd's been very good.

"I've not been to Germany this year, apart from Berlin and Frankfurt, so it's only the third time they've seen me.

"Obviously I want a good reception because I want to be doing European Tours next year in Germany.

"Whereas if they're not good to me, then I won't go. But so far, so good, and with the way I'm playing, hopefully they like it and I can produce maybe a bit better tomorrow."

Littler will play Krzysztof Ratajski, who beat Kevin Doets 10-8, in the quarter-finals on Sunday.

Earlier, Van Veen fell to a 10-6 defeat by Luke Woodhouse in the last match of the afternoon session.

Woodhouse, who threw a nine-darter in his first-round win, had a three-dart average of 95.34 compared with Van Veen's 91.47 and hit six 180s.

He will play Ross Smith in the last eight after his fellow Englishman beat Damon Heta 10-7.

Gerwyn Price also made it through with a 10-4 victory against Cameron Menzies and will face Stephen Bunting.

Bunting played Kim Huybrechts, who won his first-round match after coming in as a late replacement for the ill Luke Humphries, and was a comfortable 10-3 winner.

Jonny Clayton overcame Josh Rock 10-8 and will play Martin Schindler, who was a 10-4 victor against Jermaine Wattimena.

articles.title: Luke Littler still on course to win European Championship Darts after second-round win over Nathan Aspinall
articles.summary: The Nuke secures the second highest three-dart average in the history of the tournament as he powers into quarter-finals; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund.

Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer.

Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10.

"I felt really good from the off," Littler told ITV.

"I knew the start was good. I was gutted at giving him a leg and going into the first break at 4-1 when I wanted 5-0.

"Nathan is always there and is always going to come back at you. I couldn't afford to drop off. I felt confident and had to get the job done."

Littler arrived at this tournament following shock defeats at the World Series of Darts and the World Grand Prix which ended his dreams of a perfect season in the majors.

However, he remains on track to win the European Championship for the first time after exiting in the last 16 of his debut campaign last year.

"I'm playing well. I'm feeling really good. There was only one issue in there, but other than that the crowd have been really good," he added.

"I've had a long time off and past results haven't gone my way. I've seen on social media some memes that 'Luke's finished' and this and that.

"I've had long enough to look at them, get on the practice board and forget about it all. Hopefully if I do lift the trophy I can say I've not gone anywhere.

"I've definitely not gone anywhere here with that performance."

Littler will face Krzysztof Ratajski in the quarter-finals after the Pole fought from behind to beat Kevin Doets 10-8.

Ratajski lost the first four legs of the match and trailed 8-6 in the closing stages before clinching four legs in a row to seal a victory over the man who stunned Michael van Gerwen in round one.

Home favourite Martin Schindler kept alive his hopes of winning the title in Dortmund as he powered to a 10-4 win over Jermaine Wattimena.

The German averaged just 90, but relied on finishing stats of more than 52 per cent - including a brilliant 121 in the ninth leg - and the support of a raucous crowd to reach the last eight on home turf for the first time.

He will face Jonny Clayton on Sunday after the Welshman beat Josh Rock 10-8 in the final match of the day.

Clayton wasted a series of match darts in the closing stages, but clinched the win in brilliant fashion with a 121 checkout on the bullseye.

Afternoon session: Van Veen's reign ended by Woodhouse

In the afternoon session, Luke Woodhouse ended Gian van Veen's reign as European champion, as he coasted into the quarter-finals with a 10-6 victory.

Woody will face top seed Ross Smith on Sunday in a bid to reach the semi-final after the 2022 European champion held off a Damon Heta fightback.

A scintillating start saw Smith average in excess of 112 to storm into a 5-0 lead before Heta rallied, only to succumb to a 10-7 loss. Smith finished with six 180s and an average of 96.19.

Gerwyn Price averaged 95.75 to reach the quarter-finals for the first time in three years with a dominant 10-4 victory over Cameron Menzies, which included three ton-plus finishes.

It was tight after seven legs which all went with throw, but 'The Iceman' shifted through the gears to pull clear, winning seven of the last eight legs.

Stephen Bunting produced a finishing clinic (56 per cent) to defeat Kim Huybrechts and reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 2014.

'The Bullet' hit 10/18 on the doubles and four ton-plus checkouts to set up a blockbuster showdown with Price on Sunday.

If Price wins the title this weekend, he will provisionally be ranked higher than Luke Humphries, who withdrew from this event through illness. That would open up the possibility of a Luke vs Luke semi-final at the World Darts Championship.

articles.title: Oregon Football Falls Flat Against Illinois, Loses 21-10
articles.summary: The Ducks looked utterly lifeless in the second half, scoring zero points
articles.body:
Oregon sputtered to arguably their worst defeat in the Dan Lanning era in losing the third game that they were favored to win. The Ducks looked great on the first drive of the game, and played miserably the rest of the way. They scored zero points in the second half, where Illinois' ball control dominated the clock and gave the Ducks no hope of staging a comeback.

Illinois won the toss and deferred, giving the Ducks the first possession of the game. Oregon marched down the field, using 11 plays to get to the endzone for their first score. The rushing game was working on this drive, taking pressure off Dylan Raiola to have to do everything. The drive was capped by Jordon Davison 's 2 yard rush into the endzone.

The Illini's first drive yielded a first down and then sputtered with no gain on a third and 7 at their own 39-yard line. Illinois punted and Oregon's second drive started on the 28-yard line. This time the Ducks went three-and-out. On Oregon's 36-yard line, Illinois got pressure on Raiola and the pass attempt was incomplete, forcing the Ducks to punt. The 48 yard punt pushed Illinois to their own 16-yard line.

Illinois got to midfield on a pair of big plays. They went no further, getting zero yards on three plays, and punted into the endzone, so the Ducks took the ball again at their 20-yard line. Oregon returned the favor, going 3-and-out after Hudson Lewis dropped what would have been a huge first down pass.

Illinois could not get anything going on their next drive. After a Teitum Tuioti sack on 2nd down, Illinois punted and Oregon's next drive started on their 38-yard line. On third and 11, Raiola was sacked for a fumble, and Illinois recovered on Oregon's 30-yard line.

But, with a great short-field opportunity, The Illini could not protect quarterback Michael Clayton II, and Tuioti sacked Clayton again.

This forced a fumble, which Matayo Uiagalelei recovered, and Oregon had a first down 19 yards up the field from where they fumbled. A pass to Dakorien Moore brought us to the end of the first quarter. Oregon – 7, Illinois – 0

The Ducks lost steam at the Illinois 32-yard line, failing to convert on 2nd and 2 and 3rd and 2. They also failed to convert a 52-yard field goal, which had the distance but sailed right of the goal post. Illinois then started their first drive of the second quarter on their 34-yard line.

Illinois started their next drive on their 34-yard line and picked up a first down to get to midfield. There, Tuioti sacked Clayton for a third time and three plays later the Illini were forced to punt on 4th and 8. The punt pushed Oregon deep in their own territory on the 9-yard line.

On 3rd and two, Jordon Davison broke through a couple of tackles for a huge 32 yard gain. On 2nd a 6 at the Illinois 47-yard line, it was Dierre Hill Jr. 's time to shine, with an explosive 41 yard run. The Ducks could not quite push the ball to the goal line, and Oregon settled for a field goal on 4th and goal and the Illinois 2-yard line. Oregon – 10, Illinois – 0

After a touchback, Illinois began their next drive on their 20 with 2:29 left in the first half. One play was all it took for the Illini to run for 75 yards and pick up a touchdown. Oregon – 10, Illinois – 7

For as much as the Ducks talk about winning the middle 8, they definitely were failing on this point. Another 3-and-out drive forced the Ducks to punt, pinning Illinois deep on their own 18-yard line. The Illini called Oregon's 3-and-out with one of their own, and also punted. The Ducks started the last drive of their half on their 30-yard line with 0:37 left on the clock. Oregon got to midfield but ran out of time, and we went into halftime with the Ducks up 10-7.

At the half, Oregon had 230 total yards to 127 for Illinois. The Ducks' passing game was anemic, with Dylan Raiola going 13-20 for 96 yards, but only passing for 35 yards in the second quarter. Oregon's rushing game was doing well, with explosive plays accounting for Jordon Davison rushing for 71 yards and Dierre Hill Jr. rushing for 66 yards.

Illinois got the ball to start the second half, and it was like Oregon put a different defense on the field. Illinois ran and ran – they ran eight times in a row to the Oregon 9-yard line and then passed the ball for an easy touchdown. Oregon – 10, Illinois – 14

Oregon's offense looked as hapless as the defense, as the Ducks crawled to another three-and-out and punted the ball. The Illini started their next drive on their 20-yard line.

Illinois only made it to midfield on their next drive, but they continued to chew up the clock. They punted the ball and the Ducks started deep in their own territory, at their 9-yard line. They could only make it to midfield, and the third quarter ended with the Ducks punting to start the fourth quarter and down four points.

After the punt, the Illini started on their 7-yard line. They made a couple of first downs, but had to punt on 4th down and 8. Oregon started their first drive of the quarter on their 19-yard line.

The Ducks pushed to the Illinois 39-yard line on the strength of their rushing game, and rushing allowed Oregon to pick up a critical 4th down conversion. But the Ducks could only get a handful of yards after that, and Oregon missed their second field goal of the day with a 53 yard attempt.

Illinois looked like they might get stopped in their own territory, but a 33-yard run put them on Oregon's side of the field and they followed with a 23-yard touchdown pass. The Ducks were hopelessly out of reach of a win. Oregon – 10, Illinois – 21

Oregon got the ball with 2:29 left in the game. They reached the Illinois 28 and could do nothing, missing the third field goal of the day. Oregon would get another possession with 27 seconds left, but also got nowhere. That took us to our 21-10 final score.

Oregon had 426 total yards to 314 for Illinois. The Ducks were horrible on third down, going 4-15 for 27%.

Dylan Raiola passed 27-41 for 246 yards. Dakorian Moore was the leading receiver, with 9 receptions for 70 yards. Jamari Johnson had 7 receptions for 69 yards, and Hudson Lewis had 5 receptions for 68 yards.

Oregon rushed for 180 yards, with Jordan Davison rushing for 92 yards on 11 carries and Dierre Hill, Jr. carrying the rock 13 times for 83 yards.

articles.title: Clemson senior defensive tackle named game time decision ahead of big game
articles.summary: Ahead of Clemson’s matchup against Virginia Tech we have an injury update on defensive tackle Vic Burley.
articles.body:
Clemson will have to wait until closer to kickoff to determine whether defensive tackle Vic Burley can play against Virginia Tech.

Burley was designated a game-time decision on the ACC's final availability report ahead of Saturday's matchup at Memorial Stadium . He had been listed as questionable on each of the previous two reports, leaving his status unresolved entering the evening.

The change to Burley's designation was Clemson's only update on the final report. His availability gives the Tigers one remaining question along the defensive front as they prepare to return to conference play.

Virginia Tech, meanwhile, will be without starting cornerback Thomas Williams. The Hokies initially listed Williams as questionable when the first availability report was released Wednesday, but he has since been ruled out.

His absence leaves Virginia Tech without a starter in its secondary against a Clemson offense looking to establish more consistency through the air.

The Tigers enter the matchup at 4-2 overall and 2-1 in ACC play following last weekend's 37-0 victory over Charleston Southern. Virginia Tech brings a 5-2 record and a 2-2 conference mark into Death Valley after defeating Georgia Tech .

Clemson's homecoming matchup against the Hokies is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday on ESPN.

AUSTIN — To avoid the program's first three-game losing streak since 2021, the No. 19 Texas Longhorns need to beat the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium.

That will require a better performance from Texas senior quarterback Arch Manning, who is in danger of getting benched if he struggles early in the game , the type of decision that head coach Steve Sarkisian rarely makes with his starter.

Two players came off the pregame injury report for Texas — sophomore offensive lineman Jackson Christian (questionable) and freshman running back Derrek Cooper (probable) — but junior safety Kobe Black was added as a game-time decision.

articles.title: Lens beat PFC in Ligue 1 matchday impacted by social unrest
articles.summary: Paris FC missed the opportunity to go top of Ligue 1 as they went down 2-1 at Lens on Saturday in a matchday heavily impacted by the protests taking place ac...
articles.body:
Paris FC missed the opportunity to go top of Ligue 1 as they went down 2-1 at Lens on Saturday in a matchday heavily impacted by the protests taking place across France.

Florian Thauvin and Thorgan Hazard scored in the final 30 minutes as last season's French Cup winners came from behind to beat Paris FC.

The result condemned PFC to remaining joint on 14 points with five other clubs at the top of the table.

Lens now sit just one point behind them in sixth place.

Luca Koleosho opened the scoring two minutes into first-half stoppage time at the end of a crisp counter-attack.

The 22-year-old picked the ball up on the left flank near the Paris FC area, before driving up the pitch and exchanging a one-two with Lassine Sinayoko and finishing crisply from the edge of the box.

PFC thought they had a numerical advantage to go with their one on the scoreboard early in the second half when Lens defender Jean-Clair Todibo was given his marching orders for a challenge on Ilan Kebbal.

But VAR intervened to find the PFC attacker was offside earlier in the action and Todibo returned to complete Lens' complement.

Thauvin, a 2018 World Cup winner with France, showed his pedigree just after the hour as he drove in on his left foot and fired home from 22 yards.

The 33-year-old combined with Hazard as the Belgian netted the winner for Lens with a left-footed strike inside the box on 83 minutes.

"This isn't anything new. In many matches this season, he's got us out of tricky situations, and again today, he did what only Florian Thauvin can do -- so that's great," Hazard said.

"He's a good leader, a good captain. He carries the team."

It was the sole Ligue 1 match of the day after champions Paris Saint-Germain had their home meeting with Lyon pushed back to Monday.

The postponement of the PSG game on Friday came after a decision was taken earlier in the week to postpone another French top-flight football game, in the south-western city of Toulouse between the home team and Troyes, from Saturday to Sunday.

Games in France's second-tier Ligue 2 have also been moved this weekend on the request of police.

Police deployed resources elsewhere as French authorities braced for another weekend of protests in the capital and across the country after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.

The trouble broke out on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities to prevent further violence.

Lille visit Monaco, Marseille host Le Havre and Rennes welcome Strasbourg, alongside three other fixtures, in a jam-packed Sunday.

Second-placed PSG then take on league leaders Lyon on Monday, with a winner likely to go outright top.

articles.title: SMU Explodes in Second Half to Rout California 59-20
articles.summary: Mustangs Pull Away After Halftime The SMU Mustangs delivered a dominant second-half performance on Saturday, defeating the California Golden Bears 59-20 at G...
articles.body:
The SMU Mustangs delivered a dominant second-half performance on Saturday, defeating the California Golden Bears 59-20 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. After a competitive opening half, SMU erupted for 42 unanswered points after halftime to secure an impressive Atlantic Coast Conference victory.

Head coach Rhett Lashlee's team improved to 6-1 overall and 4-1 in ACC play, continuing its strong start to the 2026 season. The Mustangs used an explosive rushing attack and timely plays from quarterback Kevin Jennings to overwhelm California after the break.

California initially gave SMU a challenge, opening the scoring with a 10-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele to Chase Hendricks. SMU responded with a field goal from Brendan Baird before Jennings connected with Kendrick Raphael on a 22-yard touchdown pass to put the Mustangs ahead 10-7.

The Golden Bears continued to apply pressure in the second quarter. Mason Mini scored on a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Towns McGough added two field goals to help California take a 20-17 lead into halftime.

SMU answered with a one yard touchdown run from Raphael, tying the game at 17-17 before California's final field goal restored its advantage.

Whatever adjustments Lashlee made at halftime worked immediately. Christian Rhodes scored on a five-yard run early in the third quarter to put SMU back in front. Jennings then connected with Derrick McFall for a 21 yard touchdown, extending the lead to 31-20.

Rhodes added another rushing touchdown later in the quarter, giving the Mustangs a commanding 38-20 advantage entering the fourth.

SMU continued piling on points in the final period. Raphael scored his second rushing touchdown of the afternoon, while Jennings found Jalen Hale for a 17 yard touchdown pass. E.J. Kelly capped the scoring with a 10-yard rushing touchdown, completing the Mustangs' remarkable second-half surge.

Jennings finished with 223 passing yards and three touchdown passes, while Raphael rushed for 104 yards and contributed two touchdowns on the ground. SMU finished with 491 total yards, including 255 rushing yards, and held California to 40 yards on the ground.

The victory gives SMU valuable momentum as it continues its conference schedule. After allowing 20 first-half points, the Mustangs' defense shut California out over the final two quarters.

For the Golden Bears, the defeat drops them to 3-5 overall and 2-3 in ACC play. California will need to regroup quickly, while SMU can take confidence from a complete second-half performance.

articles.title: Mississippi State’s Kamario Taylor exits Oklahoma game after injury scare
articles.summary: Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor was forced to leave Saturday’s contest against the Oklahoma Sooners after sustaining a lower-body injur...
articles.body:
Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor was forced to leave Saturday's contest against the Oklahoma Sooners after sustaining a lower-body injury in the first half. It's brutal timing, as Taylor just returned for this matchup after missing the program's 31-0Week 7 loss to the LSU Tigers.

The injury happened in the first quarter when the sophomore quarterback was tackled out of bounds while scrambling for about three or four yards. Taylor was seen limping along the sidelines before going to the locker room with trainers.

Unfortunately, Taylor will not be returning to the Week 8 matchup against Oklahoma, as Mississippi State ruled the star quarterback out for the remainder of the game, according to Pete Thamel of ESPN. Backup Parker Puckett will finish the rest of Saturday's contest.

"Kamario Taylor has been ruled out for the rest of the game," Thamel reported.

The 19-year-old signal-caller finished the day with just 10 passing yards, completing just two of his five attempts. As previously mentioned, Taylor entered this game against Oklahoma bouncing back from a lower-body injury. Mississippi State will conduct further evaluation before determining whether or not this is a new injury or if Taylor aggravated a previous injury.

Taylor began the campaign as one of the hottest quarterbacks in college football . However, injuries have derailed his production ever since. Including Saturday's outing, the Mississippi State star has accumulated 1,460 passing yards, 17 passing touchdowns (SEC-high for now), while completing 66.2% of his pass attempts. His 290.0 passing yards per game average is still the highest in the SEC. He's also rushed for 147 yards and one score.

articles.title: F1 United States GP: Kimi Antonelli takes pole with George Russell sixth
articles.summary: Antonelli will become F1 world champion this weekend if he wins the race and title rival and team-mate Russell finishes ninth or below
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has claimed his seventh pole of 2026 at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, defeating Max Verstappen in a thrillingly close qualifying session in Austin.

Antonelli surged to pole with his first of two Q3 runs, which yielded a 1m34.035s as he headed Red Bull tandem Verstappen and Isack Hadjar by around two tenths, as few frontrunners improved on their final lap.

It was Antonelli's first pole since the summer break as he denied Verstappen a third consecutive pole, breaking this weekend's trend of Verstappen and the two Ferraris looking to have a slight edge on Mercedes across the demanding 5.5km Circuit of the Americas.

After impressing in practice and leading the way in Q2, Leclerc only managed fourth when it mattered, with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton in fifth.

George Russell was a disappointing sixth ahead of McLaren duo Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris , who lost two spots after seeing his final lap deleted for track limits.

Meanwhile, Racing Bulls pairing Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson further helped their squad's bid to cement fifth in the standings.

With Lindblad facing a five-place penalty for taking a new combustion engine, Lawson opted to sit out Q3 to minimise the damage for his team-mate. Lawson will start ninth anyway now, with Lindblad set for a start from 14th.

Leclerc headed Q2 with a 1m34.198s on his second run, beating Antonelli and Russell as well as an early Verstappen benchmark.

The battle for the remaining Q3 spots featured Piastri, who couldn't string a good first lap together and needed a second effort to move up to sixth after taking provisional 10th. Lindblad and Lawson also found late improvements to move into the top 10 in a dramatic end to the segment, knocking out the Alpine and Audi cars.

So Pierre Gasly was the first driver to miss the cutoff by just 0.022s for Alpine, ahead of Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto , with Franco Colapinto , Fernando Alonso and Oliver Bearman also eliminated. Haas man Bearman saw a lap that was quick enough for 13th scratched for track limits at Turn 11.

Bortoleto is facing a back-of-the-grid start for taking a new Audi power unit anyway, but the Brazilian advanced to Q2 to try and hand Hulkenberg a valuable slipstream on COTA's long straight. Alpine's Colapinto will be docked 10 grid places for installing new engine control electronics, joining Bortoleto on the back row of Sunday's grid.

Q1 - Double Williams exit while Norris goes fastest

Norris led the way in a tight Q1 session by setting a 1m35.029s, with the reigning world champion conducting two runs to cement his place, heading the four cars from Ferrari and Red Bull.

Behind them, Antonelli and Russell, as well as the second McLaren of Piastri, all advanced using a set of medium tyres, saving a set of softs.

In the background, Alonso's strong 1m36.240s lap got him through to Q2 in 16th at the expense of Haas man Esteban Ocon and his Aston Martin team-mate Lance Stroll , who lamented a lack of rear grip.

Aston Martin's improved performance relegated Williams to F1's slowest team outside of newcomer Cadillac. Carlos Sainz headed a frustrated Alex Albon in 19th, while 21st-placed Sergio Perez again had the measure of Cadillac team-mate Valtteri Bottas .

articles.title: Brett Pesce scores go-ahead goal as Devils beat Kings 3-1 for 3rd straight win
articles.summary: (AP) — Brett Pesce scored the go-ahead goal and Jake Allen made 12 saves as the New Jersey Devils beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-1 on Saturday for their third...
articles.body:
NEWARK, N.J. (AP) — Brett Pesce scored the go-ahead goal and Jake Allen made 12 saves as the New Jersey Devils beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-1 on Saturday for their third straight win.

Anthony Mantha and Artemy Gritsyuk also scored for the Devils, who also beat Colorado and Anaheim on their current homestand. New Jersey has won five of six. Allen improved to 5-2-0 this season.

Scott Laughton scored for Los Angeles, which saw its two-game winning streak snapped. Forsberg made 23 saves.

Pesce beat goaltender Anton Forsberg at 8:08 of the third period after the defenseman found a clear lane through traffic in the Los Angeles zone. Luke Evangelista and Gritsyuk assisted on Pesce's first goal this season.

Before the game, the Devils introduced newly acquired goaltender Connor Hellebuyck . The 33-year-old Hellebuyck won 345 games in 11 seasons with Winnipeg and is a three-time winner of the Vezina Trophy.

New Jersey included goaltender Nico Daws, who won against Anaheim on Thursday, in the trade for Hellebuyck on Friday. Remi Poirier, who has yet to play an NHL game, dressed as Allen's backup on Saturday.

Laughton scored at 15:57 of the second, driving the puck past Allen for his second goal.

Mantha tied the game about three minutes later with his third goal.

Gritsyuk scored his team-leading sixth goal into an empty net at 18:55.

The Kings had a power-play chance when New Jersey's Timo Meier was called for tripping at 12:59 of the third but were unable to tie the game.

Los Angeles was coming off road wins over Washington and the New York Islanders to start its five-game trip after losing its first six games.

DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Tyler Jefferson threw an 19-yard touchdown pass to Rickie Shaw II with 40 seconds left to help Bethune-Cookman beat Jackson State 24-21 on Saturday to move into a tie atop the Southwestern Conference standings.

Jefferson was 8-of-13 passing for 113 yards and three touchdowns and added 68 yards rushing on 19 carries for Bethune-Cookman. Deanwar Johnson had nine carries for 81 yards.

On third-and-11, Jefferson rolled to his left, then back to the right before he hit Shaw along the right sideline in the end zone for the go-ahead touchdown .

articles.title: Why did NC State fire Dave Doeren? Wolfpack make change in wake of loss to Stanford
articles.summary: Doeren had been with the Wolfpack since 2013.
articles.body:
NC State lost 31-28 to Stanford on Friday night, a result that was apparently enough for the Wolfpack to make a coaching change.

Less than 24 hours after the result, NC State announced it fired long-time head coach Dave Doeren amid the 3-4 season. Doeren was one of the longest-tenured head coaches in the country, as he had been in Raleigh since the 2013 season.

In Doeren's spot, special teams and running backs coach Todd Goebbel will take over the team on an interim basis. Goebbel has been at NC State since 2019 and has never been a head coach in any capacity.

Here's more on why NC State fired Doeren.

NC State fired Doeren on Saturday following a loss to Stanford on Friday night, marking the Wolfpack's fourth of the season. That puts NC State just one loss away from matching its total from all of 2025, yet the team is still five wins away from reaching last year's eight-win mark.

"I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," AD Boo Corrigan said . "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role."

Doeren had been at NC State since 2013, producing losing seasons just three times but never reaching 10 wins in any season. The Wolfpack seemingly decided that it was time to move on from Doeren after over a decade of similar results.

articles.title: OFA swimmers finish NAC season with victory
articles.summary: Having a meet decided on the final event of the season was nothing new for the OFA girls swimming team. In fact it was a fitting way to end the season Friday...
articles.body:
Having a meet decided on the final event of the season was nothing new for the OFA girls swimming team.

In fact it was a fitting way to end the season Friday when the Blue Devils' 400 freestyle relay won the final event of the day and carried OFA to a 62-59 victory over Massena. It was the Blue Devils' third win of the season and all three were decided by the final races. Another meet ended in a tie and another ended as one-point loss to Gouverneur.

"Close meets like this are very exciting for the girls and to get three wins and a tie was a very good season for a team so small in numbers. I made a little change to the lineup and we had a very good relay team for the final race," said OFA Coach Andee West.

Colbie O'Shea built a sizeable lead as the first swimmer of the relay and Chloe Frank, Jaylin Wannemacher and Jordyn Dobbs maintained the comfortable margin. Following the meet, Coach West expressed her pride in her team which took on the challenge of sustaining the program.

"This season has been one of the toughest beginnings I've ever faced, but in true swimmer fashion, we persevered. Our little family stuck it out together and faced every single obstacle head on! We had so many more wins than what's on a paper… the personal growth that I saw before my eyes daily was inspiring," she wrote. "I'm a proud coach. I'm a grateful coach. I'm a lucky coach. We ended the regular season on a win. We have many heading to Sectionals, they worked really really hard for this. We'll be back next year in the meantime we'll also be working hard in TRIBs."

Winning relay members contributed to the OFA victory. Dobbs and O'Shea swam on the winning 200 medley relay team with Vada Knapp and Emmy Lowry; Wannemacher led the 100 freestyle in 1:32.5; Lowry won the 200 individual medley relay in 2:48.76; Frank led the 100 freestyle in 2:40.59 and O'Shea took second in the 500 freestyle where Massena's Tori Cusworth took a pool record time of 5:41.61 and eased the previous record of 5:42,46 of OFA swimmer Terri Dranger set in 2004.

Cusworth also led the 100 breaststroke in 1:17.52 and swam on the winning 200 freestyle relay with Aaliyah Prashaw, Zoey Thomas and Millie St. Louis. Massena also earned first place points from Prashaw in the 50 freestyle and 100 backstroke and St. Louis in the 100 butterfly.

Vital seconds and thirds for OFA came from Wannemacher and Frank in the 50 freestyle, Emmy Lowry and Jordyn Dobbs in the 100 breaststroke, Vada Knapp in the 100 backstroke and the 200 IM, Jordyn Dobbs in the 100 butterfly and Madyson Thomas in the 100 freestyle.

articles.title: McAfee's late goal lifts undefeated Winnacunnet past Londonderry in D1 quarterfinal
articles.summary: "It's just been such a fun season and we're not ready for it to end yet," Winnacunnet field hockey head coach Heidi Hand after 2-1 quarterfinal win over Lond...
articles.body:
HAMPTON - With less than four minutes remaining in Saturday's Division I field hockey quarterfinal, top-seeded Winnacunnet was deadlocked at 1-1 with No. 8 Londonderry. Then senior forward Fiona McAfee delivered the moment Winnacunnet needed most.

McAfee raced nearly the length of the field and blasted home the go-ahead goal with 3:35 remaining, lifting the Warriors to a 2-1 victory at Winnacunnet High School.

"It feels really, really good," McAfee said. "Honestly, I'm happy about how the game went. I think we needed to realize that you have to work really hard in the playoffs because it's not easy. Records don't matter anymore. We have to play strong the entire game."

The victory sends Winnacunnet (16-0) into the Division I semifinals, where it will face No. 4 Bedford on Wednesday at 7 p.m. at Exeter High School. The Bulldogs advanced with a 4-1 victory over No. 5 Merrimack.

"It's just been such a fun season and we're not ready for it to end yet," Winnacunnet head coach Hand said.

"We went to the semis last year, and I think it definitely helps that a lot of our players were on the team last year," McAfee said. "So, a lot of people have felt what it feels like to go to the semifinals. I know for me, I already feel a little less nervous going to the semis; I feel more pumped up than nervous, which I think is good."

McAfee said Londonderry challenged the Warriors throughout the afternoon.

"They're a strong team, and they matched us for a lot of the game," McAfee said. "But we came out stronger."

Hand expected nothing less from the Lancers. The Warriors defeated Londonderry 1-0 during the regular season and knew the rematch would be equally competitive.

"I'm just so happy for everyone," Hand said. "They played so hard as a team today and never backed down. We started off a little slow, and we knew it'd be a battle right from the start. I'm so proud of them. They don't let up."

McAfee's game-winner was exactly the spark the Warriors needed.

"She's such a remarkable player," Hand said. "Her skill, her passion. I knew she'd leave her heart out there today."

Senior Sofia Donatelli gave Winnacunnet a 1-0 lead with the game's first goal in the second quarter, and that advantage held through halftime. Londonderry answered with a third-quarter goal.

"I think everyone definitely turned it up a notch," junior defender Mary Kouloheras said of the team's response after the equalizer.

McAfee credited Winnacunnet's teamwork for creating its scoring opportunities.

"Our team does a good job working together to finish," she said. "Our goals wouldn't happen if we didn't connect and pass with each other."

The Warriors' defense also came up with several key plays down the stretch. Kouloheras made a critical defensive save late in the game to preserve the tie before McAfee's winner. Winnacunnet goalie Riley Gagalis was credited with three saves.

"Mary had a defensive save coming out of nowhere," Hand said. "The entire defensive unit stayed together back there. They all worked hard, kept their sticks low, communicated and had Riley's back."

Hand said her message throughout the second half was simple - don't panic.

"That was our biggest thing, just don't let up," Hand said. "We know Londonderry is a team that fights right to the end."

Kouloheras said the victory was a reward for months of hard work.

"I was just so relieved because I know we really deserve it," she said. "Everyone has been working so hard and giving 100 percent, so it's a good feeling."

articles.title: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat from Patriots vs. Bears
articles.summary: Let’s use Mike Vrabel’s categorizations to break down the Patriots’ loss in Week 7.
articles.body:
Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team's performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead.

The New England Patriots are now 0-2 in prime time games this season. The second of those defeats came on Thursday night at the hands of the Chicago Bears, a 30-24 loss in what was a competitive game between two good teams. At the end of the day, though, it was the home team that ended up making more plays.

With that said, let's dive into our weekly breakdown of the good and the not-so-good from the loss at Soldier Field.

Even though his early-season version reared its head again at one point, Drake Maye looked every bit like the franchise-caliber quarterback he is on Thursday. In fact, the entire pass game operation was pretty good against the Jets: two touchdowns plus 310 net yards and 9.4 per play, and that's not even including 26 yards on three scrambles.

From top to bottom, New England moved the ball well whenever it took to the air. Of course, that was largely due to Maye.

"He gave us a chance. He competed," said Mike Vrabel. "I know he'd like to have that throw back to Eli [Raridon], but I thought he really competed. Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football, he gave us a chance. I know he'd like to have that one back and he'll learn from it like he always does. I'm glad he's ours."

On the day, Maye completed 77.4% of his pass attempts for 321 yards, a pair of touchdowns and that interception in the end zone. Even putting that play into account, he finished with 0.34 expected points added per play — the same number as his Bears counterpart, Caleb Williams.

Maye is the main man, but the operation also function the way it did because of the blocking up front. Even with guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown out (let alone Mike Onwenu), New England surrendered only 14 quarterback disruptions for a 38.9% pressure rate — the third-best mark of the season thus far.

"We protected when they pressured," said Vrabel. "I thought that was a huge key for us as they continued to pressure and put a lot of guys on the line of scrimmage. Our ability to pick it up and hit some chunk plays was really the reason we were in it in the second half."

"We didn't run the ball well enough," was Mike Vrabel's blunt assessment after the game. And he was right, the Patriots didn't.

Excluding those aforementioned Drake Maye scrambles but including a quarterback sneak for no gain, the Patriots finished with only 44 yards on 14 carries for an average of 3.1 yards per run and -0.40 expected points added per run. As a reminder, the Bears defense had entered Thursday ranked just 25th in the NFL, giving up an average EPA of -0.057.

So, what was the issue? Unsurprisingly given the circumstances, it started up front: New England's run blocking simply was too spotty to make a consistent difference. When it worked well the results looked the part (see: Rhamondre Stevenson's 13-yard carry in the second quarter) but when it didn't there simply was no room for the backups to operate (see: the very next play).

Given that the Patriots had to overhaul their O-line on a short week, struggles like that had to be expected. But the breakdowns were not only due to Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor entering the lineup, but across the board — including at tight end and wide receiver. One potential big TreVeyon Henderson run, for example, was unable to develop because center Jared Wilson was beat climbing to the second level; meanwhile, Eli Raridon's run blocking continues to be a mixed bag.

Add it all up, and you get the Patriots not getting anything going on the ground.

The s—t that gets you beat: Big-play defense

Leading up to the game, we mentioned "limiting explosive runs" as a key to the game for the Patriots. To their credit, they did that, and were only beaten twice by a team averaging close to four explosive per game entering the contest; those two plays furthermore only barely earned "big play" status by gaining precisely the 10 yards required for that classification.

But while New England did a good job in that area, stopping big plays was an issue throughout the evening on Thursday: the Bears finished with 10 of them, meaning that eight happened in the passing game and on plays gaining 20-plus yards.

Among those was a 58-yard catch-and-run and 24-yard touchdown, both to wide receiver Luther Burden. The Patriots struggled to defend the second-year man all game: he was responsible for four of those eight explosive passing plays, gaining 130 yards total on those.

To make matters worse, three of the explosives — including Burden's touchdown — came in third-and-long situations and only one came on first down. On average, the Bears were 11.6 yards off the line to gain on their big passing plays. Those situations do invite a vertical pass game, but this also shows how New England's defense kept putting itself in favorable situations only to allow the Bears to nonetheless wiggle their way out of them.

There are a multitude of issues why New England gave up that many big plays in the passing game. Some were just excellent execution on the offense's part; some were apparent communication breakdowns at the second and third levels; some were the result of insufficient tackling and New England missing a combined 17 of 81 tackle attempts for a rate of almost 21%.

No matter the reason, the performance in that area simply wasn't good enough.

The Penn State Nittany Lions have landed the second running back they were looking for, securing a commitment from three-star running back Jordan Hall on Saturday, according to Hayes Fawcett of Rivals .

He is ranked as the No. 820 overall player and No. 64 running back in the Rivals industry ranking. The 5-foot-10, 200-pounder is also the No. 31 player from Ohio.

Hall missed his junior season with an injury, but has been excellent as a senior, leading Princeton High School to a 10-0 record. He has 1,179 rushing yards and 24 touchdowns and counting.

Penn State now has 22 players committed in its 2027 recruiting class, the first full cycle under head coach Matt Campbell. Hall is their second commitment at running back, joining Chukwuma Odoh, another three-star product. articles.title: 5 thoughts on Indiana football’s 13-6 win over Michigan
articles.summary: From Josh Hoover’s play to a better day on the ground, here’s some quick takeaways from the win over the Wolverines.
articles.body:
Indiana football moved to 7-1 overall and 4-1 in Big Ten play on Saturday afternoon with a nailbiter of a 13-6 win over Michigan in overtime.

It was the Hoosiers' first win over the Wolverines in Ann Arbor since the 1967 season, the program's first ever Rose Bowl appearance. There were plenty of concerning points, particularly on offense, but a few things to feel good about.

There's a lot being said about Josh Hoover right now and the reality is this: he wasn't good enough today. He also wasn't 100% today.

Hoover still looks like a guy recovering from the apparent shoulder injury he suffered against Ohio State last week. He completed just eight of his 18 attempts through the air on the afternoon as Indiana struggled to get the passing game going.

He made the play when it mattered though, finding Brock Schott in overtime for a deep connection before running the ball in himself to score the only touchdown between either team on the game.

There's going to be more to say about Hoover soon, but for now it's probably worth cooling off a tad.

Indiana's running game struggled mightily against both of Nebraska and Ohio State coming into this game. There was plenty to worry about between Indiana's offensive line not getting enough push through the middle and how that could affect the passing game.

It wasn't quite a get right game, the Hoosiers were still below the standard established earlier this season, but you'll take 3.7 yards per carry as a team after the last two weeks.

Both Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. managed rushes of over 10 yards, with the latter going for a strong 4.7 yards per carry. The offense needs to keep that production going on the ground in the coming weeks with Minnesota looming before a bye week.

The defense will keep Indiana in every game

Bryant Haines' unit has been the difference between this team and a worse record for the most part, limiting opposing offenses for several quarters as that of Indiana figures itself out in winning time. That deserves a ton of praise.

There were low moments, like Stephen Daley jumping over the line to give a Michigan drive life, but Indiana's playing as well as any team on that side of the ball right now.

Indiana, through two and a half seasons under Curt Cignetti, has made the big plays in the biggest moments far more often than it hasn't.

Coming off of perhaps the most notable instance when it hasn't, Indiana's offense responded in a major way in overtime between the deep pass to Schott and Hoover using his legs to get into the endzone. That's not even mentioning all the work the defense did in the shadow of its own goal to keep Michigan from taking the lead this afternoon.

That was a hallmark of last year's team and it's just part of this program's DNA. "Never Daunted" is more than just a saying to these guys.

Between Hoover's health and a need to get back into a groove offensively, Indiana is in dire need of the bye week.

Unfortunately for Indiana, Minnesota sits between it and said bye week. The Hoosiers have to get through the Golden Gophers to get some much-needed rest. That's gonna be eight straight games, truly Indiana's pretty fortunate to not be more banged up than it already is.

articles.title: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua. Adams is out,...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday's practice.

That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup.

The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua's status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Davante Adams ' absence makes Puka Nacua 's status more consequential

Adams' absence is settled, but the supplied report does not identify his injury or provide his practice progression. His status should therefore be separated from Nacua's documented calf issue rather than treating both situations as identical.

Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury's severity or confirm he will miss kickoff.

His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active.

Nacua's production illustrates what is at stake. The Rams list him with 37 receptions for 417 yards and one receiving touchdown across four appearances this season. That represents substantial production to potentially remove from an already depleted receiving group.

If Nacua plays, Los Angeles must balance using its remaining centerpiece with whatever workload he can handle. If he sits, the passing game requires a broader redistribution rather than simply transferring Adams' opportunities to one replacement.

Where the injuries leave the Rams' offensive approach

The most sensible adjustment would be to prioritize manageable situations rather than demand that replacement receivers consistently win difficult matchups.

That could mean leaning on the running game, using play-action and creating shorter completions through formations and route combinations. Those are potential solutions, not confirmed changes to the game plan.

The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere.

Colby Parkinson offers some reassurance. The tight end practiced fully Wednesday, Thursday and Friday despite a shoulder injury and carries no game designation.

He also enters this matchup after catching five passes for 31 yards and a touchdown against Arizona, according to his official game log. That recent involvement makes him worth watching as Los Angeles considers how to distribute opportunities.

Still, increased tight-end usage cannot automatically replace everything Adams and Nacua provide. The Rams need complementary contributions, efficient protection and fewer wasted downs rather than expecting one player to absorb the entire burden.

Defensive concerns increase the importance of offensive efficiency

Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings.

Josh Wallace provides better news, practicing fully throughout the week with a calf injury and receiving no game designation.

Alaric Jackson, Byron Young and Aaron Donald missed Friday for designated rest and have no game designations. Those entries should not be confused with the injury-related absences.

For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams' absence reduces its options, and Nacua's availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. Los Angeles needs a sustainable plan for either outcome, not an assumption that questionable means ready for an unrestricted workload.

articles.title: Britain's Smith retains title in split-decision win over Puello
articles.summary: Britain's Dalton Smith defends his WBC light-welterweight world title with a split-decision victory over Alberto Puello in a triumphant homecoming in Sheffie...
articles.body:
Britain's Dalton Smith defended his WBC light-welterweight world title with a split-decision victory over Alberto Puello in a triumphant homecoming in Sheffield.

The 29-year-old extended his unbeaten professional record in a high-class tactical contest at the Utilita Arena, with both fighters displaying sharp counter-punching skills.

The result hung in the balance as the judges' scorecards were read out, with victory for either man or a draw seemingly possible.

But Smith edged it, with two judges scoring the contest 115-113 in his favour and the third awarding it 116-112 to Dominican fighter Puello.

It was Smith's first title defence after his stunning fifth-round knockout of Subriel Matias in Brooklyn in January.

"We knew it wasn't going to be a show, he was going to be an awkward opponent, but a champion has to do what he has to do," Smith said post-fight. "These are the best in the world and I'm proving why I'm number one now."

The Sheffield fighter passes another stern test against two-time world champion Puello to extend his record to 20 wins.

With his mandatory challenger out of the way, Smith keeps his dream of headlining Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough Stadium alive and will target some of the biggest names in boxing, including unbeaten American Shakur Stevenson.

"I have a lot of respect for Shakur - he's one hell of a fighter," Smith added. "But this takes me back to the Ricky Hatton and Mayweather days. We can build something good."

Promoter Eddie Hearn added: "Dalton Smith is a legacy guy. I know that money plays a big part in boxing, and we want to make sure that this guy lives a wonderful life.

"First and foremost this guy is a real fighter, who wants belts, legacy, and to make his city proud."

Sheffield has a rich boxing history, having produced world champions including Prince Naseem Hamed, Johnny Nelson and Kell Brook, and those in attendance gave their latest champion a hero's welcome.

Wearing the blue and white of his beloved Sheffield Wednesday, he made his ring walk to AC/DC's Thunderstruck.

The contest began cagily, with neither fighter willing to overcommit as both showed sharp defensive skills.

Smith had beaten the fearsome puncher Matias by standing and trading, but Puello posed a different challenge - a slick southpaw relying on movement and counter-punching.

The champion dictated the pace in the early rounds. He landed a right in the fourth, but Puello, 32, found his range with his left before Smith connected again just before the bell.

Puello - whose only career loss came against Matias last year - came alive in the sixth, landing a series of straight lefts to take the round. The challenger then slipped to the canvas, briefly raising hopes of a knockdown among the home crowd.

The atmosphere resembled a football terrace, with a drummer and trumpeter accompanying fans singing Sheffield Wednesday songs.

A superb double jab and right hook from Smith in the ninth was answered by an uppercut and hook to the body from Puello, showcasing the quality of both fighters.

With the contest - originally scheduled for June before an elbow injury forced Smith to withdraw - finely poised, both men had everything to fight for heading into the championship rounds.

Cut below his right eye, Smith traded blows with Puello, perhaps edging the exchanges through his higher work-rate.

Smith played to the crowd in the final 20 seconds, before leaping into his father's arms at the final bell.

Is Stevenson next - and could Smith headline Hillsborough?

Smith's breakthrough year has established him among the leading fighters at light-welterweight. He had already won British, Commonwealth and European honours, and a successful first world-title defence further strengthens his credentials.

"Tonight, for me, Dalton Smith cemented himself as the number one pound-for-pound fighter in Britain," Hearn added.

The biggest challenge could come against Stevenson, the unbeaten WBO world champion and a four-weight world title-holder. The American is widely regarded as one of boxing's most gifted technicians.

Stevenson's recent departure from Zuffa Boxing could open up opportunities for negotiations, while another potential unification opponent is WBA champion Gary Antuanne Russell.

Closer to home, a meeting with unbeaten British rival Adam Azim has been discussed for several years. The pair have exchanged words throughout their rise and Smith has indicated he would welcome the contest at Hillsborough in 2027, although he believes Azim still has work to do before challenging for his world title.

"Number one goal in my life was to become world champion and make history, the second was to sell out Hillsborough stadium," Smith added.

The prospect of Smith defending his title in front of tens of thousands of supporters at the home of his boyhood football club would be another remarkable milestone.

Smith is not one for trash talk or the theatrics that often help fighters build their profiles, preferring to let his performances do the talking.

But the challenge now is turning world-title success into high-profile fights that could catapult him into the mainstream.

The Denver Broncos have placed outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the next four games.

articles.title: Devils cap off perfect homestand with 3-1 win over Kings
articles.summary: Brett Pesce scored the go-ahead goal and Jake Allen made 12 saves as the Devils beat the Los Angeles Kings, 3-1, on Saturday for their third-straight win.
articles.body:
NEWARK, N.J. (AP) — Brett Pesce scored the go-ahead goal and Jake Allen made 12 saves as the Devils beat the Los Angeles Kings, 3-1, on Saturday for their third-straight win.

Anthony Mantha and Artemy Gritsyuk also scored for the Devils, who also beat Colorado and Anaheim on their current homestand. New Jersey has won five of six. Allen improved to 5-2-0 this season.

Scott Laughton scored for Los Angeles, which saw its two-game winning streak snapped. Anton Forsberg made 23 saves.

Pesce beat Forsberg at 8:08 of the third period after the defenseman found a clear lane through traffic in the Los Angeles zone. Luke Evangelista and Gritsyuk assisted on Pesce's first goal this season.

Before the game, the Devils introduced newly-acquired goaltender Connor Hellebuyck . The 33-year-old Hellebuyck won 345 games in 11 seasons with Winnipeg and is a three-time winner of the Vezina Trophy .

New Jersey included goaltender Nico Daws , who won against Anaheim on Thursday, in the trade for Hellebuyck on Friday. Remi Poirier , who has yet to play an NHL game, dressed as Allen's backup on Saturday.

Laughton scored at 15:57 of the second, driving the puck past Allen for his second goal.

Mantha tied the game about three minutes later with his third goal.

Gritsyuk scored his team-leading sixth goal into an empty net at 18:55.

The Kings had a power-play chance when New Jersey's Timo Meier was called for tripping at 12:59 of the third but were unable to tie the game.

Los Angeles was coming off road wins over Washington and the New York Islanders to start its four-game trip after losing its first six games.

articles.title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Responds to New Development After Getting Benched
articles.summary: After barely seeing any action in the New York Giants’ 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6, running back Cam Skattebo appears poised to get ample...
articles.body:
After barely seeing any action in the New York Giants' 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6, running back Cam Skattebo appears poised to get ample touches again.

The former Arizona State Sun Devils star running back appears to be back in the mix after a "good week" of practice, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN

"It's been good, you know. I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo said, via Raanan. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball."

Giants' Skattebo is Back in the RB Mix Ahead of Week 7 Game

Skattebo led the Giants in rushing yards in each of their first five games of the season, but his fumble in Week 5 apparently led to a major decrease in his role the following week against the Saints.

Instead, it was New York newcomer quarterback JJ McCarthy , who led the team on the ground in the Saints game, and he only had 26 rushing yards.

After releasing Najee Harris, New York now features a running back room with Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary.

The 24-year-old Skattebo only has 294 rushing yards and a touchdown on 81 carries this season, and seems aware that he's not exactly lighting it up on the field.

"I didn't do anything yet," Skattebo shared. "I took care of the ball during practice, and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I'm going to give it everything I've got."

New York will face the Houston Texans on the road at Reliant Stadium in Houston this coming Sunday, looking to end its two-game winless streak and improve its NFC East-leading 3-2-1 record.

articles.title: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli earns surprise pole for the US Grand Prix as he chases the F1 title
articles.summary: AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Kimi Antonelli earned a surprise pole position Saturday for the United States Grand Prix, giving the championship leader a chance to clo...
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Kimi Antonelli earned a surprise pole position Saturday for the United States Grand Prix, giving the championship leader a chance to close out the season title with a victory if his closest rivals falter.

Mercedes' 20-year-old Italian driver edged out Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who came to the Circuit of the Americas having won the previous two races from pole position.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar will start third. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who looked like a pole contender most of Friday and Saturday, will start fourth.

Antonelli will be chasing his ninth victory of the season. And he has a mathematical chance of winning the championship.

First he must win. If he does that, and Mercedes teammate George Russell finishes ninth or lower, and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishes outside the top four, Antonelli will clinch the championship. He would be the youngest champion in F1 history.

Hamilton will start fourth, with Russell sixth.

Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points and Hamilton by 111 with six races left in the season. He built the large lead through the first half of a remarkably consistent season that included five wins in the first six races.

He hadn't started on pole since Belgium, a span of seven races.

Of the 13 previous races at COTA since 2012, 11 winners have started on the front row. The exceptions were Leclerc from fourth in 2024 and Verstappen from sixth in his dominant 2023.

articles.title: Battle of the Owls: Florida Atlantic storms back to defeat Rice 51-49
articles.summary: Easton Messer is the only FBS player in the last 20 seasons with two rushing touchdowns, two receiving touchdowns and a punt return touchdown in the same gam...
articles.body:
BOCA RATON – A wild homecoming victory over Rice has put Florida Atlantic one win away from bowl eligibility for the first time since 2020.

Despite giving up over 600 yards of offense, FAU scored seven touchdowns - three rushing, three passing and on special teams - to defeat Rice 51-49 on Saturday.

FAU (5-2, 2-1) still had difficulty stopping Rice's (1-7, 0-4) running game, going down 14-0 early in the first quarter. However, the home team fought back, passing for more than 300 yards, forcing a turnover and a safety and going 4-for-4 in the red zone in a key shootout victory.

"At the end of the day, we had to find a way to get the stop. They got down the field late, we got the stop and that's what I'm proud of," FAU Coach Zach Kittley said.

The dynamic duo of Caden Veltkamp and Easton Messer continued to shine Saturday afternoon, Veltkamp throwing for 331 yards and three touchdowns. Veltkamp threw an interception at the end of the first half, but he also had a QB sneak for a touchdown.

"I have to be smart with the football there because if we scored there at the end of the half, then we go out up 2 scores and we get the ball coming out and we have a chance to go up 3 scores," Veltkamp said. "But other than that, and the first drive, I played well for 3 quarters for the most part.

But the real star was Messer, who tied a school single-game record with five touchdowns. He was all over the place as he ran the ball from the backfield, lined up at wide receiver and returned punts and amassed 262 all-purpose yards.

Messer had 12 catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns on three carries and even returned a punt 82 yards for his second return touchdown of the season.

Per @ESPNInsights, Messer is the only FBS player in the last 20 seasons with two rushing touchdowns, two receiving touchdowns and a punt return touchdown in the same game.

"I'm never surprised by anything that he does," Veltkamp said. "He works harder than anybody I've ever been around. I'm super proud that he got to display all facets of his game today."

Even after his historic performance, Messer was still critical of himself.

"It's kind of weird 'cause I think simultaneously, it felt like one of the worst games I played personally and one of the best," Messer said. "The stats were good, but I started the game with some uncharacteristic drops. I really just looked at that as an opportunity to lead by example, and show my teammates that it really is the next play mentality. Just make plays whenever they come your way,"

Kittley was moved to tears talking about Messer postgame.

"He's such a selfless football player," Kittley said. "He doesn't really care how many touches he gets, he just wants to win. And I trust him a lot. He can do everything for your team, man."

FAU also spread the wealth. Kelby Valsin caught seven passes for 78 yards, and Branden Hoch started FAU's comeback with a 30-yard touchdown reception in the first quarter, the first of his career for the former West Boca standout.

"He's a guy that you're going to look out for the next couple years," Kittley said of Hoch. "Hopefully he stays here with us, man. He's going to be a 75- to 80-catch guy in a year or two. I believe that about him."

FAU's run defense has plagued it all season, going back to Week 1 when the Owls gave up 281 rushing yards in a loss to Florida. That negative trend continued when they gave up 246 rushing yards the next week against Navy.

After a few strong defensive performances, the run defense is struggling again. After allowing 479 rushing yards to Army two weeks ago, Florida Atlantic allowed 467 rushing yards against Rice.

Rice QB Gael Ochoa ran for 259 yards and four touchdowns. Ochoa had 19 rushing yards on the season before Saturday's game.

The competition only gets stronger. FAU will not play a team with a losing record the rest of the season with a Thursday night game at North Texas up next.

"We're lucky we got a noon kick (against Rice). We can get our guys more time to rest and recover and our coaches more time to game plan," Kittley said. "We've got to practice, but I also have to make sure our players are healthy and fast for Thursday."

articles.title: UCF Knights pull off stunning upset over undefeated BYU in mind-boggling overtime thriller
articles.summary: UCF Knights stunned the No. 2 BYU Cougars in double overtime in Orlando, delivering the biggest win over a ranked team in their program history.
articles.body: It has been a wild couple of weeks in college football, but what happened on Saturday in Orlando — a UCF Knights double-overtime win over the BYU Cougars — might be the craziest thing yet. After a big win over Notre Dame and Top 10 teams dropping like flies last weekend, the BYU Cougars found themselves coming into Week 8 at No. 2 in the nation. On Saturday, they headed down to Orlando, Florida, to take on Scott Frost's UCF Knights. BYU QB BEAR BACHMEIER SAYS NOTRE DAME 'DISRESPECTED' HIM AND HIS FAMILY FOLLOWING UPSET WIN OVER IRISH The 3-3 Knights have struggled in the Big 12 since joining the conference, but tend to be better at home in the friendly confines of the Acrisure Bounce House. The Cougars opened the scoring when quarterback Bear Bachmeier hit wide receiver Kyler Kasper for six. But UCF managed to hold them through the rest of the first quarter and then answered with a touchdown of their own in the second, when Knights running back Landen Chambers broke through a notoriously solid BYU defensive line on the goal line. After forcing BYU to punt, UCF managed to drive deep into Cougar territory, but failed to get into the endzone. They settled for a field goal attempt on fourth-and-goal. While kicker Will Stone got the job done to give the Knights a 10-7 lead, the decision to play it safe drew boos from the home fans. They may have had a point because Bachmeier lowered his head and burst into the end zone on the following possession. UCF ended the half with another red zone drive coming off of an interception, only this time they didn't have to settle for a field goal. QB Keyone Jenkins found Chambers through the air for six. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE That plus an extra point meant that UCF took a 17-14 lead to the locker room at halftime. This was the third time they led or were tied with a ranked opponent at the half this season, but went on to lose both games. In the second half — with rain falling — BYU scored on their first drive, but UCF answered right back to regain their three-point lead. BYU settled for a field goal to tie the game at 24-24. A couple of drives later, a short punt gave UCF good field position with 8:50 left in the game. What followed was an 11-play drive that set up a fourth-down play on the goal line. The Knights held the Cougars deep in their own end, but they flipped the field with a booming punt ahead of UCF's final drive of regulation. Johnson then led the offense downfield and into kicker Will Stone's field goal range. On second-and-ten, it appeared that Jenkins had fumbled and it was recovered by BYU; however, upon review, it was overturned and ruled an incomplete pass. On top of that, BYU defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa was assessed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that gave the Knights a fresh set of downs and moved them up to the BYU 28-yard line. After a few plays to bleed time off the clock, UCF brought out the kicking unit on third down, but the kick was blocked and recovered behind the line of scrimmage. With Stone's helmet coming off and no flag on the play, the half came to an end because of a ten-second run-off, and it was off to overtime. UCF won the toss and elected to get the ball second. On third-and-13, Bachmeier hit Legend Glasker to put the Cougars ahead. But it didn't last long because on UCF's first play, Jenkins scrambled for his life, then found receiver Josh Derry in the endzone. The PAT was good, and the OT continued. Stone returned and kicked a field goal, but BYU's Kendal Wall was called for roughing the kicker, giving the Knights a fresh set of downs, and it only took two plays for Jenkins to hit tight end Grayson Brousseau — who grew up fifteen minutes from Provo — for the touchdown, and then was successful on the mandated two-point attempt. In their second OT possession, BYU's undefeated season and No. 2 ranking came down to a single play, and UCF managed to hang on for the biggest win over a ranked team in program history. That throws a huge wrench into the rankings and playoff picture, and it had the potential to rejuvenate UCF's season as they go to 4-3 with a signature win under their belt. Kalani Sitake's Cougars will now look to bounce back on Halloween against the Arizona State Sun Devils, while the UCF Knights will move on to face Baylor.

articles.title: Team USA hero Connor Hellebuyck discusses the difference between playing hockey in US and Canada
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck says he's "really excited to play hockey again" after sitting out all season and addresses New Jersey Devils media for the first time.
articles.body: The NHL was rocked by a massive trade on Friday that saw the Winnipeg Jets deal three-time Vezina Trophy winner, Olympic gold medalist and soon-to-be Medal of Freedom recipient Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils. The goalie hasn't played so far this season after asking for a trade over the summer, but now that it's done, he's gearing up to hit the ice and has addressed the New Jersey media for the first time. "Sitting at home for so long was getting to me. For myself, I’m just really excited to play hockey again," Hellebuyck said on Saturday, per the Associated Press. "I’m joining a very skilled group. They brought me for a certain specific role. I’m really excited to fill that role, not only on the ice but off the ice as well." SOCIAL MEDIA REACTS TO EXCRUCIATINGLY AWKWARD MOMENT BETWEEN DEVILS JACK HUGHES AND ESPN ANALYST The Devils are off to a good start this season with a 7-4-0 record after Saturday's win over the Los Angeles Kings, during which netminder Jake Allen was between the pipes. Adding a goalie of Hellebuyck's caliber to the lineup could mean that goals will be at a premium for any team that plays the Devils. But for Hellebuyck, it will be different playing in New Jersey compared to a Canadian market like Winnipeg, something he was asked about. UTAH'S MACKENZIE WEEGAR REACTS TO AMERICAN PLAYERS SEEKING TRADES OUT OF CANADA: 'IT’S A BIT UNFORTUNATE' "I mean, it's a catch-22; some people love that," he said of playing in markets where people bug players about hockey while they're trying to grocery shop. "Sometimes you just want to be left alone. Canada loves their hockey, and I felt that to the bone, and I loved my time there, and I've loved the people I've met. Made a lot of good friends and built good relationships there." "So, I can't say that one is better than the other," he continued. "I know that I've enjoyed both and I've experienced both. It's just one of those things that's part of hockey culture... they love their hockey, and we love our hockey in our own way, and that should be celebrated."
