articles.title: Asian Para Games bronze leaves Suhas Yathiraj hungry for gold amid IAS duties and badminton
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.IAS officer by day, shuttler by nightFor most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Lee Chong Wei's influenceSuhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India returned from the Asian Para Games in Nagoya with its best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, powered by world records, golden doubles and medal-winning
articles.body: India returned from the Asian Para Games in Nagoya with its best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, powered by world records, golden doubles and medal-winning debuts. TOI picks out the ones who stole the show...MONA AGARWAL: A golden double and a world recordMona Agarwal won the women’s 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold before setting a world record in the 50m rifle three positions SH1. Her score of 357.5 secured a second title and made her the first Indian para-shooter to medal in the event. The Jaipur-based Paris Paralympics bronze medallist trained for the 50m event with a rented rifle, travelling long distances to train.PRANAV SOORMA: Two titles, two recordsPranav Soorma claimed the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 gold with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m, then added the club throw F51 title with a Games-record 32.87m. Paralysed after a spinal cord injury at 16, Soorma rebuilt his life through education and sport. His Nagoya double followed club throw gold at the previous Asian Para Games and silver at the Paris Paralympics.NISHAD KUMAR: Two disciplines, two gold medalsNishad Kumar ventured beyond his high jump speciality to win the men’s T47 long jump with an effort of 7.11m, then claimed high jump gold with a Games-record clearance of 2.04m. The double Paralympic silver medallist took on the additional discipline despite a troublesome knee, showcasing his versatility.SIMRAN SHARMA: Silver to goldSimran Sharma won the women’s 200m and 100m T12 titles, improving on her two silvers at the previous Games. articles.title: No. 15 Florida State soccer takes first ACC loss against No. 17 Notre Dame
articles.summary: The ‘Noles took their first ACC loss of the season in a ranked matchup.
articles.body:
No. 15 Florida State women's soccer fell 2-0 to No. 17 Notre Dame on Saturday night in Tallahassee, ending the Seminoles' two-game winning streak.

With the loss, Florida State took its first conference loss and fell to 7-2-3, while Notre Dame improved to 7-1-6.

Florida State's starting 11 included Shaneil Buckley, Wrianna Hudson, Sam Erbach, Peyton McGovern, Joelle Jung, Nyanya Touray, Nawreen Ahmad, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke, Grace Hoytink and Kate Ockene.

The Seminoles struggled to create offensive opportunities in the first half, while Notre Dame was able to take an early lead.

The Fighting Irish opened the scoring in the 15th minute, taking a 1-0 lead.

Notre Dame continued to control much of the first half, finishing with five shots, including two on goal, while FSU was unable to record a shot before halftime.

The Fighting Irish carried their momentum into the second half, with Izzy Engle scoring just 47 seconds into the second half to extend Notre Dame's lead to 2-0.

Florida State began creating more offensive opportunities shortly after, with Tanner Strickland recording the Seminoles' first shot on goal in the 48th minute.

Hoytink had another opportunity in the next minute for FSU, but her shot went just wide to the left.

Buckley also created a scoring opportunity, but her shot was blocked by Notre Dame's defense.

In the 64th minute, Ahmad found Hudson with a pass that led to another shot opportunity for the Seminoles, but FSU was unable to convert.

Hudson continued to pressure Notre Dame's defense, coming close to scoring with a header in the 82nd minute that missed the goal.

Despite creating more opportunities in the second half, Florida State was unable to find the back of the net.

The Seminoles finished with six shots, including three on goal, while Notre Dame recorded eight shots, with four on goal.

Florida State will look to bounce back when it hosts Duke on Thursday, Oct. 29, with kickoff set for 8 p.m.

articles.body:
New York Road Runners hosted TCS New York City Marathon Kids Kickoff events in Brooklyn, the Bronx, Queens and Staten Island as part of the lead-up to the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon on Nov. 1.

The nonprofit organization expanded the youth event across all five boroughs for the first time, staging five events over two days as part of a yearlong celebration of the 50th anniversary of the original five-borough New York City Marathon course.

Events at Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 6, St. Mary's Park, Astoria Park and Ocean Breeze Park were expected to draw 2,000 children participating in races, dashes and family-friendly activities.

The festivities are scheduled to continue Sunday, with 3,000 children anticipated in Central Park alone.

According to New York Road Runners, the TCS New York City Marathon Kids Kickoff is the organization's premier and largest youth event. The program features nearly 5,000 youth athletes of all abilities, ranging in age from 2 to 18.

The events are being held one week before 60,000 athletes are expected to compete in the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon on Nov. 1. New York Road Runners described race day as the "best day of the year" in the "best city in the world."

The 2026 TCS New York City Marathon takes place on Sunday, November 1. Coverage on Channel 7 and wherever you stream ABC 7 New York begins with pre-race coverage, Marathon Sunday, at 7:00 a.m. Live coverage of Sunday's marathon begins at 8:00 a.m. only on Channel 7 and ESPN2.

articles.title: Morgan Whittaker scores in 81st minute and the Rapids beat the conference-leading Whitecaps 1-0
articles.summary: (AP) — Morgan Whittaker scored in the 81st minute, Nico Hansen made two saves for his ninth clean sheet of the season, and the Colorado Rapids beat the Vanco...
articles.body:
COMMERCE CITY, Colo. (AP) — Morgan Whittaker scored in the 81st minute , Nico Hansen made two saves for his ninth clean sheet of the season, and the Colorado Rapids beat the Vancouver Whitecaps 1-0 on Saturday night to extend their home unbeaten streak to 10 matches.

Whittaker headed in his third goal of the season after Vancouver goalkeeper Yohei Takaoka deflected Donavan Phillip's shot off the crossbar and it fell to the Rapids forward at the back post.

Colorado (12-13-6) snapped a five-game winless streak with its first victory since Sept. 12. The Rapids entered having played to a tie in their last three games.

Vancouver (16-8-7) lost for the second time in its last five games. The Whitecaps still sit atop the Western Conference standings, one point ahead of Dallas.

Takaoka, who entered with 13 shutouts this season, finished with seven saves.

Vancouver: Returns home to play San Diego on Wednesday.

Colorado: Plays at San Jose on Wednesday.

articles.title: Jokic has triple-double, Murray scores 42 points in Nuggets' OT victory over Pelicans
articles.summary: DENVER (AP) — Nikola Jokic scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the short-handed Denver Nuggets rallie...
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — Nikola Jokic scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the short-handed Denver Nuggets rallied from down 23 to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 on Saturday night.

Jokic had his 199th career triple-double in the regular season, second to Russell Westbrook, who retired with 209.

Jamal Murray scored 42 points and rookie Trevon Brazille had seven of his 17 points in overtime in his home debut for Denver, which took an early lead in overtime. His corner 3-pointer with 1:25 left in overtime gave the Nuggets a 133-129 lead.

Denver played without Cam Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist) and continued to be without Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones.

Trey Murphy III led New Orleans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22 points and Derik Queen and Zion Williamson scored 17 each. The Pelicans have dropped their first three games under first-year coach Jamahl Mosley.

The Pelicans got some welcome news when center Yves Messi's knee injury suffered Friday night in Utah is a contusion and not something more severe.

New Orleans shot 65.9% in the first half and led by 23. Denver rallied to cut it to 16, and Jokic and Murray combined to score 22 of the Nuggets' 32 points in the third quarter but the Pelicans extended the lead to 19 heading into the fourth.

Denver erased the deficit on 3-pointers from Murray and Jokic, a reverse dunk from Aaron Gordon, and then had a chance to go ahead with 17 seconds left but Murray made two of three free throws to tie it.

Pelicans: Host Denver on Wednesday night.

Nuggets: Host Golden State on Monday night.

The first period of the game didn't see a single goal despite chances on both ends of the ice, but the second frame wouldn't be the same case.

Scoring just 20 seconds apart were Sean Walker and Jesperi Kotkaniemi – Walker's goal assisted by Jackson Blake for his 100th career NHL point.

articles.title: Rockets’ Alperen Sengun rattles the rim with insane slam dunk vs. Hawks
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets are flying high after their dramatic win over the San Antonio Spurs, which saw them improve to 2-0. They had sights set on win No. 3 Sat...
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets are flying high after their dramatic win over the San Antonio Spurs, which saw them improve to 2-0. They had sights set on win No. 3 Saturday against the Atlanta Hawks, and Alperen Sengun was more than doing his part.

Early in the third quarter, the Turkish big man decided to take the ball down the court against "The Great Barrier Thief" himself, Dyson Daniels. Sengun then decided to do it all by himself as he drove past Daniels and threw down a slam dunk through traffic.

Sengun has had a strong start to the season for the Rockets. Over the first two games, he's averaged 26.0 points, 8.5 rebounds and 6.0 assists . And he kept up his fine overall play against the Hawks. He finished with 17 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists to lead the Rockets to a 121-114 win.

Point guard Fred VanVleet was rested on the second night of a back-to-back , but the newfound balance in the Rockets offense continued against Atlanta. Seven Houston players had 11 or more points, led by Kevin Durant's 22.

The return of VanVleet has been a welcome addition to Sengun, who no longer has to have quite as much responsibility as a facilitator on offense. But as he showed with his amazing drive and dunk against the Hawks, he is still more than capable of calling his own number and putting the ball on the floor at times.

The Rockets will take on the Hawks again, this time in Atlanta, for the second half of their home-and-home on Monday.

articles.title: Arch Manning, Texas barely save soap opera season with thrilling Ole Miss victory
articles.summary: It wasn't pretty or easy, but the Longhorns are still alive in the hunt for the CFP, and Arch Manning still has his starting job.
articles.body:
Arch Manning crossed his arms after a TD run with fireworks exploding in the background. He stomped around the sideline in defiance. He walked into the end zone for the go-ahead TD.

Manning delivered the gotta-have-it game with No. 19 Texas on the brink, even if it was dicey after a second-half comeback by No. 7 Ole Miss. The Longhorns survived in a 34-27 victory.

So, this is what we get after Texas coach Steve Sarkisian described Manning as "edgy" this week? It is worth the experience, right?

Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC) jumped out to a three-TD lead on the Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC). Manning finished 18 of 30 for 212 yards and three total TDs, albeit with two interceptions and a fumble. He summed up that experience in the postgame interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe. MORE: Which of the SEC 7 two-loss teams has best chance to make CFP?

"I think all week we just said, 'Whatever it takes,' and got the win," Manning said. "I think you need to start doing our games more. We're 3-0 with you this year."

Those three games were decided by a combined total of seven points. The Longhorns held off a furious comeback led by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who finished 25 of 52 for 250 yards, two TDs and three interceptions. Chambliss tried to tie the score on the game's final play, but Jelani McDonald, who had the pass breakup on a Hail Mary in the 20-17 victory against Tennessee on Sept. 26, came up with the game-clinching interception.

Manning and Texas remain the soap opera of the 2026 season, and this was yet another cliffhanger for the two-loss Longhorns in the jumbled SEC playoff race. MORE: Meet Arch Manning's entire extended family

Arch Manning leads Texas to huge halftime lead

Here is what we learned after the Longhorns' victory. Backup quarterback KJ Lacey, who was rumored to be in the mix for more first-team reps in the aftermath of Texas' 27-24 loss to Florida in Week 7, will not be the starter this season. Lacey played one snap after Manning took a hard hit in the third quarter.

Manning transfer rumors, as they have for the past four years, will fizzle again. Manning could still enter the 2027 NFL Draft and be a first-round pick. Texas' season-long script with Manning, in all its drama, is far from finished.

Manning took his own advice and "let it rip" against the Rebels. That started in the first quarter with a 43-yard pass to Ryan Wingo and a 23-yard run by Raleek Brown, who trucked Ole Miss safety Joenel Aguero on the run. Manning scored on a 2-yard run and struck a pose in the end zone.

Manning was not finished. A 19-yard scramble by Manning set up a 50-yard TD pass to Wingo for a 17-3 lead with 12:38 left in the third quarter. Michael Terry III added a 3-yard TD run to extend the lead to 24-3.

Manning was 13 of 19 for 171 yards, a TD and an interception in the first half. Chambliss was 6 of 18 for 63 yards and two interceptions, including a fourth-and-goal interception to Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles with 1:37 left in the half. This looked like the game where Manning would silence all the critics. MORE: Where does Steve Sarkisian rank among CFB;s highest paid coaches?

This is Texas, after all, which was coming off losses to Oklahoma and Florida the last two weeks. The Sooners and Gators outscored the Longhorns 37-14 in the second half over the last two weeks.

Manning lost a fumble on a sack by Blake Purchase, which Kam Franklin recovered in the end zone at the 13:28 mark in the third quarter. The Rebels trimmed the lead to 24-17 on a 6-yard TD pass from Chambliss to Horatio Fields with 6:46 left in the third quarter. The Longhorns had just two first downs in the third quarter.

That set up the fourth quarter. Chambliss tied the score with a 27-yard TD pass to Fields with 13:57 left in the fourth quarter.

Texas answered with a six-play, 80-yard drive that came exclusively on the ground. Brown had a 47-yard run up the middle, which was the Longhorns' first chunk play of the second half. Terry had runs of 19 and 12 yards, respectively, and Manning walked in a 1-yard TD on a bootleg with 8:04 remaining.

Alex January blocked an Ole Miss field-goal attempt, and Gianni Spetic gave Texas a 34-24 lead on a 33-yard field goal with 2:25 remaining.

You knew it wasn't over. Lucas Carneiro kicked a 39-yard field goal, the Rebels recovered the ensuing onside kick and Chambliss nearly led a game-tying drive before the final interception.

"I was pacing and said a few prayers, but our defense came up clutch," Manning said. "That's what it's all about." MORE: How a bad day for the Big 12 impacted hurt league's CFP outlook

The Longhorns still have issues. Edge rusher Colin Simmons (ankle) and running back Hollywood Smothers (shoulder) missed Saturday's game. Tackle Trevor Goosby was carted off with an injury in the first quarter, and receiver Cam Coleman left with a shoulder injury in the third quarter. Texas had 14 penalties for 134 yards.

Yet if the College Football Playoff rankings came out Tuesday, the Longhorns would probably be in the top 12 based on victories against Ole Miss, No. 3 Ohio State and No. 11 Tennessee. No other team has three victories against teams inside the top 12 at this point.

We'll find out more over the next two weeks in road games against No. 22 Missouri and No. 18 LSU. Texas needs even more out of Manning; otherwise, the doom-and-gloom cycle will start again with a third loss. Is there a more entertaining drama in college football right now?

articles.title: O'Shaquie Foster Put On The Performance Of A Lifetime — Now History Is 1 Fight Away
articles.summary: O’Shaquie Foster beat Emanuel Navarrete by unanimous decision in San Antonio to unify the WBC, IBF and WBO titles. See the full results, scorecards and fight...
articles.body:
O'Shaquie Foster just put on a masterful display of boxing at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. He dropped Emanuel Navarrete twice in the 12th round en route to a dominant unanimous-decision victory (118-108x2, 115-111). On paper, this fight looked like it had a chance to be the Fight of the Year.

Instead, it turned out to be one of the best in-ring performances in 2026 by a single fighter. Now, Foster is one fight away from becoming the undisputed champion at 130 pounds — which is something that has never been done in boxing.

Foster simply picked Navarrete apart. He exposed the Mexican's sloppy feet and slow hands and he did it fighting primarily in the pocket. Here is a look at some of his handiwork.

O'Shaquie Foster def. Emanuel Navarrete, unanimous decision

Foster retained the WBC title and won the IBF and WBO titles

Foster 26-3 (12 KOs), Navarrete 40-3-1 (33 KOs)

How Did Fighters React to O'Shaquie Foster's Win?

Fighters throughout the sport took to X with reactions.

Foster even got acknowledgment from the fighter he's been chasing for more than a year.

Foster was stellar and he looks every bit the part of a pound-for-pound talent in the sport. With his win on Saturday, Foster is set to face the winner of the upcoming fight between WBA champion Anthony Cacace and Nick Ball.

That would be for the undisputed title at 130 pounds. Based on Foster's performance against Navarrete on Saturday, he'd likely be the favorite against both men.

Albert Gonzalez stayed unbeaten and kept his NABF featherweight title on the main card, stopping Edward Vazquez with body shots at 1:04 of the second round. Frank Martin won the vacant NABO super lightweight title with a seventh-round TKO of Tarik Zaina.

A scheduled bout between Steven Navarro and Emanuel Moreno was canceled after Navarro missed weight.

Samuel Contreras vs. Oscar Pedroza Padilla

Foster is being mentioned as a candidate for Fighter of the Year and it makes sense. He has beaten Ray Ford and Navarrete while unifying three world titles. I don't think there is another fighter who has done more in 2026.

articles.title: ‘Disappointed!’- Kalen DeBoer calls out Alabama’s biggest problem after Texas A&M win
articles.summary: Kalen DeBoer has made his frustration with Alabama’s running game clear despite the Crimson Tide securing a much-needed victory over Texas A&M. Alabama enter...
articles.body:
Kalen DeBoer has made his frustration with Alabama's running game clear despite the Crimson Tide securing a much-needed victory over Texas A&M.

Alabama entered the matchup following consecutive SEC defeats to Georgia and Tennessee, leaving DeBoer under pressure to get his team back on track.

The win provides some relief, but the head coach knows his side must improve offensively before the final stretch of the regular season.

Kalen DeBoer demands more from Alabama Crimson Tide's struggling run game

Speaking after the victory , DeBoer praised Alabama's determination to fight for four quarters but was far less pleased with the team's ground attack.

When asked about the running game, the Crimson Tide head coach did not hide his disappointment.

"Disappointed, disappointed," DeBoer said. "The stats, that's all you gotta really look at, and we needed more out of that run game to open up some things for us."

DeBoer also highlighted missed blocks, negative rushing plays and defenders getting through the line as areas that need to be addressed.

"When we get some negative yards and have guys that are unblocked at the point of attack, or falling off blocks, those are things that we gotta get back to the basics, and we gotta get better at."

The concern is particularly relevant with young quarterback Keelon Russell leading the offence. Alabama needs a more consistent rushing threat to help create opportunities and take pressure off its passing game.

Russell did, however, earn praise for his response after some early struggles, with DeBoer highlighting several important throws late in the contest.

Wide receiver Rico Scott also impressed, making key contributions when Alabama needed someone to step up.

The Crimson Tide now have a bye week before returning to SEC action against LSU, giving the coaching staff time to work on the issues exposed against Texas A&M.

However, Alabama will also have to monitor injuries. Offensive lineman William Sanders suffered a lower-extremity injury and could miss several weeks.

The victory offers DeBoer some breathing room, but Alabama's next challenge is turning its late-game resilience into a more complete performance. Improving the run game will be a key part of that task.

articles.title: New London's Hicks edges out Colonel Crawford's Stirm in photo finish
articles.summary: In the most thrilling race of the day, it came down to a camera check to determine the winner after both finish line officials saw differing endings.
articles.body:
GALION - For most runners, a photo finish is something you only see in movies.

New London's Carter Hicks must be a movie star then, because this is his second such ending to a race in the last month.

"More than I can count," he laughed when asked how many times this has happened before. "It was the same thing at Ontario, came down to that."

Four weeks ago at the Bill Brown Invitational he was vying for runner-up honors and ended up missing it by five-hundredths of a second. At Saturday's Division IV district meet, Hicks edged out fellow junior Isaac Stirm of Colonel Crawford by fractions of a second as both crossed the finish line in 16:22.5 — the timing software didn't go past tenths of a second.

One official saw Hicks' neon green jersey cross first, another saw Stirm's black and gold. After consulting the finish line camera, they agreed Hicks won by a hair.

"I knew it was going to be a close race today because Isaac had a good race last week," Hicks said. "I knew he was gonna be right on my tail the whole race ... I feed off people pushing me and close races like that for sure.

"I knew I was the favorite to win today and if I came out here and executed, I could win today."

Stirm was hoping it would be him crossing first, though.

"My goal was to win, but it's fine because we still got next week" he said. "It pushed me a lot, he really pulled me through the race. And in my opinion, this is a pretty tough course with the hills and stuff."

Most importantly, they'll both be heading to Tiffin next weekend for the regional meet with their teammates as the photo finish also determined second and third in the team scoring — New London totaled a 94 to Colonel Crawford's 95.

"It thought it would come down to us and Crestview today and it was actually really close between us and Colonel Crawford," Hicks said. "Me winning was the difference."

Seniors Ryan Twinning (8th, 17:28.8), Fritz McCully (24th), and Trace Landis (42nd) along with sophomores Luke Fawcett (28th), Logan Stanley (39th), and Michael Hardman (47th) rounded out the team placings for New London. Seniors Landon Strausbaugh (12th) and Gordie Ekin (30th), juniors Christian Mott (21st), Wyatt Burge (51st), Grayden Bohach (57th), and sophomore Bryce Parsons (36th) made up Colonel Crawford finishers.

"I think the team is hyped for regionals and I'm really excited to go," Stirm said.

Stirm was coming off a Northern 10 championship a week earlier and had this race planned out ahead of time to near perfection even taking the lead late down the home stretch before Hicks found a final surge at the finish line.

"Isaac had a great race and that's great to see," Colonel Crawford coach Jordan Kiess said. "But it's also hard because it's like — aww dang, I didn't get him — but he has put in the blood, sweat, and tears.

"And he's very analytical … with the way his brain works. We love that … and he motivates the team as well, so we're definitely blessed to have the group of kids we do."

Crestview won a district title with a 58 led by five runners all in the top 20. Junior Isaac McFarland (16:42.8) was third, sophomore Isaac Smith (17:26.3) finished seventh, junior Logan Robinson (17:49.1) was 13th, freshman Easton Smith 18th, juniors Brandt Leigh (19th) and Jackson VanScyoc (29th), freshman Cody Wolford 49th.

Joining the aforementioned three teams are Mansfield Christian (4th, 142 points) who was led by junior David DeLorenzo (17:39.3) in ninth, Crestline (6th, 179 points) led by senior Colton Keller (17:23.9) in sixth, and Buckeye Central (7th, 181 points) paced by juniors Jeremiah Roberson (10th, 17:42.7) and Blaise Metzger (16th, 18:07.7).

Individual qualifiers include Wynford senior Evan Stacklin (14th), Bucyrus sophomore Micah Spears (17th) and senior AJ Griffin (23rd), Lucas sophomore Wilson Amert (20th), Plymouth sophomores Carter Jester (22nd) and Weston Smith (41st).

In the Division III race, six individuals are moving on to regionals. Willard sophomores Dream Mills (8th) and Riley Branham (32nd), freshman Lincoln Sallee (28th), and junior Lucas Winans (39th) along with Clear Fork senior Peyton Freitag (15th) and sophomore Hayden Maglott (31st) will race at Hedges-Boyer Park in Tiffin.

articles.title: Texas recovers after blowing big lead, hangs on to beat Ole Miss
articles.summary: Texas blew a 21-point lead before recovering in the fourth quarter to beat Ole Miss and end a two-game losing streak.
articles.body:
AUSTIN - After surrendering a 21-point halftime lead, 19th-ranked Texas rallied to score the go-ahead touchdown on Arch Manning's 1-yard bootleg run in the final three minutes and beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 to keep its SEC championship hopes alive.

The Longhorns were pushed to the limit when the Rebels scored three second-half touchdowns, including a fumble recovery in the end zone, to tie the game at 24-24 on the third play of the fourth quarter.

Texas' Alex January blocked a 58-yard field goal as Ole Miss tried to cut into its seven-point deficit. Raleek Brown, who ran for 157 yards, keyed a late drive leading to a 33-yard field goal by Gianni Spetic with 2:25 to boost the lead to 10 points.

The Rebels got within seven points with 1:22 left and then recovered an onside kick that the Longhorns couldn't corral. Texas survived after Jelani McDonald intercepted Trinidad Chambliss' pass in the end zone as time expired. The Longhorns improved to 5-2 overall and evened their SEC record at 2-2. Ole Miss fell to 5-2 and 3-2.

All but given up for dead after losses to Oklahoma and Florida, the Longhorns came out inspired and motivated, and Manning stepped up with his best performance of the year in the first half before having three turnovers to keep Ole Miss in the game.

Ole Miss' comeback to tie the game began with a sack of Manning resulting in a fumble recovery in the end zone by defensive end Kam Franklin for a touchdown. Chambliss then connected with Horatio Fields on a pair of touchdown passes of 6 and 27 yards, victimizing cornerback Kade Phillips on two perfect throws. The second score came on the third play of the fourth quarter.

The Longhorns, misfiring the entire third quarter, put together an 80-yard scoring drive to retake the lead at 31-24 with the help of a gigantic 47-yard run by Brown. Sophomore Michael Terry III, the fourth-string running back, ripped off gains of 12 and 19 yards to the lip of the goal-line before Manning scored on a perfectly timed 1-yard bootleg run.

Texas jumped out to a 24-3 in the first half with three consecutive touchdown drives and a goal-line stand for its best half of the season. But the double-digit lead for the fifth game in a row should have been much bigger.

Manning came out on fire. The junior quarterback completed 13 of 19 throws in the opening half with one touchdown and an interception. He should have had two scoring tosses, but Cam Coleman dropped an easy catch with nothing but green in front. Ryan Wingo did haul in a perfect pass for a 50-yard score.

Manning also utilized his legs for the first extended time of the season, gaining 30 yards on four runs and scoring his first touchdown of the year after running for 10 last season.

Justin Cryer stepped in front of an Ole Miss receiver for an interception - and Texas' first takeaway in SEC play - one play after Manning was picked off for the sixth time this season.

That was the first of two interceptions by the Longhorns, who ranked 102nd nationally and 13th in the SEC in turnover margin. The second came on a great read by linebacker Rasheem Biles as Texas held the Rebels out of the end zone on a long drive with its first goal-line stand of the year.
